Credit: xamdkx authored PR288 and already supplied disposable actual-server happy-path CI evidence; bdunn77 previously cautioned against public-instance demo writes. Pinned PRhead775e99be8f9c48a0e5ce5ffbc0d513088de98df7; checked current main0e47f770. I ran the complete original Python example and companion proposal as ordinary Windows subprocesses, using real urllib TCP HTTP to a disposable127.0.0.1 response fixture, not AST extraction or a substituted transport. Nineteen scenarios cover happy path, read failures/JSON shape, refused unsigned/signed writes, claim refusal, owner-readback status, mismatched owner and embedded-DID false positives. Retained results: original2/19 correct, proposal19/19, zero unexpected unittest errors; 91+57=148 HTTP requests and36+19=55 ephemeral-key signed tuples checked by unchanged official PyNaCl verification. 17 failing conditions are variants of demo failure reporting/continuation and owner matching, not17 production bugs. The narrow companion patch checks required HTTP200 statuses, validates the messages-list JSON shape, requires a full DID value line after successful owner readback, and stops with nonzero exit on failure. No automatic retry or rollback; earlier accepted writes may remain. Happy path is preserved. Patch apply, new-test/proposal Ruff lint/format under pinned project config, syntax and6 original Git blob checks pass. Boundary: controlled response/ownership fixture, deliberately including DID-bearing error bodies; not observed production responses, actual server storage/authorization/limiter/replay, cryptographic owner proof, Linux full repository tests or upstreamCI. Counts exclude development reruns. No public-service test writes, protected user key or wallet were used in these local tests. Only this authorized factual summary uses the protected existing key internally. Author adoption/main merge remain unconfirmed; no new PR or peer comment was posted.
